text: On Monday morning, the European Commission announced in Brussels that it had reached a preliminary agreement with the government of Norway on a new framework for cross-border energy trading. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told reporters that the deal, which had been negotiated over eighteen months by teams led by Kadri Simson and Norwegian minister Terje Aasland, would take effect on January 1, 2027. The announcement came two days after the International Energy Agency published its annual outlook in Paris, warning that demand for electricity in Northern Europe could rise by twelve percent before 2030. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley said the agreement would benefit Equinor and Statkraft, while executives at Siemens Energy in Munich welcomed the news. In Oslo, Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre described the framework as a milestone for the North Sea region. He was joined at the press conference by Anniken Huitfeldt and by Espen Barth Eide, who had returned from talks at the United Nations in New York on Friday. Meanwhile, in Washington, Senator Lisa Murkowski said the United States Department of Energy would study the European model during hearings scheduled for March 14. Reporters from Reuters, Bloomberg and the Financial Times noted that the agreement still required approval from the European Parliament in Strasbourg, where the vote is expected in late April. Opposition to the deal has been voiced by Marine Le Pen in France and by members of the Alternative für Deutschland in Berlin, who argue that the framework favours Norwegian exporters. Supporters, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Dutch Prime Minister Dick Schoof, countered that the deal would lower prices for consumers in Amsterdam, Hamburg and Copenhagen. The World Bank, in a statement issued from its headquarters on Tuesday, said that similar arrangements could be replicated in Southeast Asia, pointing to ongoing discussions between Singapore and Malaysia. Shares of Ørsted rose four percent on the Copenhagen exchange after the announcement, and Vestas Wind Systems gained three percent. In London, Ofgem chief executive Jonathan Brearley said the United Kingdom would open its own consultation on May 2, noting that National Grid had already begun feasibility studies with TenneT in the Netherlands. The Norwegian Sovereign Wealth Fund, managed by Nicolai Tangen, declined to comment. Later in the week, Greenpeace and Friends of the Earth organised demonstrations outside the Berlaymont building, demanding stronger protections for fisheries in the Skagerrak. A spokesperson for the Commission, Arianna Podestà, confirmed that an environmental review led by scientists from the University of Bergen and ETH Zurich would be completed by September 30, 2026, before any interconnector construction begins near Stavanger or Aberdeen.

explicit_spans.note: the pool's first min(16,P) valid spans (pool order) broadcast over Q, scored with model.score_explicit_spans(EncodedBatch from _encode_core, indices, valid_mask); logits are masked to -1e4 where explicit_mask is 0 or the span is illegal

tensor_notes.text_states: _encode_core: last_hidden_state gathered at text_word_indices, zeroed by text_word_mask
tensor_notes.query_states: _encode_core: last_hidden_state gathered at query_marker_indices, zeroed by query_marker_mask
tensor_notes.pool_indices: DocumentCandidatePool output [B,P,2] (start,end) half-open word boundaries; (0,0) where pool_mask is 0
tensor_notes.candidate_states: candidate_encoder output masked to 0 where pool_mask is 0, stored as [B,P,H]; the runtime's CandidateTensorBatch.candidate_states is this expanded to [B,Q,P,H]
